image_description: A full-body side view of an American Bison standing on a dirt path with grass and a tree trunk in the background. The bison has a massive, shaggy dark brown forequarter with a prominent shoulder hump, transitioning to smoother, lighter brown fur on the hindquarters. It has short curved horns, a beard, and sturdy legs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, showing the characteristic broad shape and short, upward-curving horns typical of a bison.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct tuft of long, dark hair hangs from the chin and throat area.
The eye is visible and appears dark, consistent with the species.
One ear is partially visible; it is small and surrounded by thick fur, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits the classic bison silhouette with a high, heavy shoulder region.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture is visibly shaggy and dark on the front half, creating the defining hump.
There is a clear visual transition from the shaggy front to the smoother, shorter-haired rear flank.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horns are proportionally small relative to the massive head and body.
All four legs are visible, appearing sturdy. The hooves are planted on the ground and appear structurally correct, though fine detail is limited by resolution.
The tail is visible hanging down, ending in a darker, bushy switch.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Bison bison) and rule out hybrid or generic bovid errors.
To verify the structural integrity of the four legs and their connection to the torso, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs.
To check for 'melting' artifacts where the shaggy fur meets the background, a common AI failure mode.
To assess general texture consistency and look for subtle noise or pattern repetition in the fur and ground.

focus_areas: Fur texture transition between forequarters and hindquarters
Leg-hoove grounding and separation from the dirt path
Boundary sharpness of the shaggy mane against the background
Anatomical correctness of the head and horn curvature
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition zone between the shaggy front fur and the smoother rear fur; AI often blurs this boundary unnaturally. Verify that the hooves do not merge with the dirt texture. Check if the eye reflects light realistically or appears flat/painted.
